title: Unable to query DuckDB file on private S3 bucket
body: When I attach a DuckDB database stored on S3 with `ATTACH 's3://bucket/path/to/test.duckdb' AS test (READ_ONLY)`, I get `Catalog Error: Cannot open database ... in read-only mode: database does not exist`. I installed and loaded `httpfs`, configured the S3 region and access keys, and reproduced this with the nightly JDBC client through DBeaver on macOS 14.2.1 on an M1. The nightly reports DuckDB v0.9.3-dev3121.

symptoms_visible: Attaching my S3-hosted DuckDB file read-only reports that the database does not exist, even after I load httpfs and configure my S3 credentials.
N0.label: N0 private S3 ATTACH failure reported

symptoms_visible: The public test database initially gives me the same missing-database error when I attach it directly from S3, while downloading that file with the AWS CLI and attaching the local copy works.
N1.label: N1 remote versus local access tested

symptoms_visible: After installing and loading httpfs on the matching build, I can attach the public test database but my database in the private bucket still reports that it does not exist.
With the same S3 credentials, I can query an Iceberg table in that private bucket, and my database becomes attachable if I move it to a public bucket.
N2_x.label: N2_x httpfs-only suggestion aftermath

symptoms_visible: On DuckDB 1.1.0, the same script can read Parquet from my private bucket but cannot attach a DuckDB database there.
N3.label: N3 failure confirmed on current release and isolated to ATTACH

symptoms_visible: Using the credential-chain secret setup, I can attach the database from my private S3 bucket.
In my AWS SSO environment, explicitly creating the secret with endpoint, key, secret, and region does not work and also prevents my read functions from working correctly.
N4.label: N4 modern credential-chain secret verified

symptoms_visible: The DuckDB database in my private S3 bucket attaches successfully with the current S3 credential-chain secret configuration, and I can query the attached database.
N_terminal.label: terminal private S3 database attach working

question_patterns: Can you try attaching the publicly accessible `s3://duckdb-blobs/data/my.db` database from a current main build?
Does the public S3 test database attach successfully in your environment?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I pulled main and tried attaching `s3://duckdb-blobs/data/my.db`, but I received the same database-does-not-exist error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The public database attaches successfully, and my private database also attaches once I use the same build.
I get the same error from a nearby main commit rather than the exact commit you used.

question_patterns: Can you download that public database through the AWS CLI and attach the local copy?
Are you able to read or list the S3 object outside DuckDB, and does the downloaded file open locally?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. `aws s3 cp s3://duckdb-blobs/data/my.db ./my.db` downloads it, and `ATTACH './my.db' AS test (READ_ONLY)` works. I can use the database and query its table.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The downloaded file also fails to attach locally with a database-format error.

edges.comment: Reporter tested the maintainer's public database on main, then demonstrated that the same object downloads through the AWS CLI and attaches locally.

solution.intent: Treat the failure as solely caused by the httpfs extension not being loaded, and install and load httpfs before retrying ATTACH.
solution.concrete_example: Run `INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;` and then retry `ATTACH 's3://bucket/path/test.db' AS test (READ_ONLY)`.

edges.comment: Actual falsified suggestion: loading httpfs makes the public database attachable but does not resolve authenticated ATTACH against the reporter's private bucket. The reporter repeated the test on the same commit and showed that other authenticated reads worked.

question_patterns: Can you retest on a current DuckDB release and show whether a `read_parquet` call and an `ATTACH` call behave differently with the same private bucket credentials?
Does this still reproduce on DuckDB 1.1.0, and can the same script read another object from that bucket?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried DuckDB 1.1.0. `read_parquet` from the same private bucket works using the same script, but attaching the database still fails. I've attached a screenshot of the run.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both `read_parquet` and `ATTACH` fail with an explicit access-denied response using the same credentials.
The same split occurs on DuckDB 1.0.0 rather than 1.1.0: reads work and ATTACH fails.

edges.comment: A later affected user supplied the DuckDB 1.1.0 comparison and screenshot; all affected reporters are folded into one simulated user side. The test isolates the issue to ATTACH rather than general private-bucket readability.

question_patterns: Please replace the legacy AWS credential-loading setup with a current S3 secret using `PROVIDER CREDENTIAL_CHAIN`, then retry the private-bucket ATTACH and report what happens.
Can you test the recommended S3 secrets configuration against the same private DuckDB file?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Huge win: I can get the private database ATTACH to work with the credential-chain setup shown in my screenshot.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The credential-chain secret still gives the same database-does-not-exist error for the private DuckDB file.
The credential-chain secret works when created as a persistent secret instead of a temporary secret.

edges.comment: Handler-initiated configuration probe, so this remains a measurement clarification even though the tested configuration is also the workaround. The target's volunteered information records that explicit static secret fields behaved differently in this user's AWS SSO environment.

solution.intent: Use DuckDB's current S3 secret mechanism with the AWS credential-chain provider for authenticated ATTACH, rather than relying on deprecated legacy credential loading; keep httpfs loaded and verify by attaching and querying the actual private database.
solution.concrete_example: Load `httpfs`, then configure credentials with a current secret such as `CREATE OR REPLACE TEMPORARY SECRET s3_auth (TYPE S3, PROVIDER CREDENTIAL_CHAIN);`. With the AWS SSO or SDK credential chain available to the DuckDB process, retry `ATTACH 's3://my-bucket/path/database.duckdb' AS remote_db (READ_ONLY);` and run a query against `remote_db` to verify it.
solution.inference_hint: The reporters supplied the behavioral contrast: public ATTACH works, authenticated reads from the private bucket work, legacy/static credential setups fail for ATTACH, and the credential-chain secret succeeds. Concluding that the missing-database message masks an ATTACH credential-path problem, rather than a missing object or corrupt database, is engineer-side inference.

edges.comment: Technical resolution reflected in the thread: migrate from deprecated legacy AWS credential loading to the current secrets API, using the credential-chain provider for this AWS SSO environment. Documentation was updated separately and is not a scored release-management requirement.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as credential configuration for authenticated ATTACH: the legacy AWS credential-loading/static setup used in the failing cases did not supply usable credentials to the private S3 database ATTACH path, despite other S3 reads working.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the public-versus-private comparison, successful authenticated Iceberg/Parquet reads, and the successful credential-chain secret probe.
Must recommend DuckDB's current S3 secrets API with `PROVIDER CREDENTIAL_CHAIN` for the demonstrated AWS SSO environment, while continuing to load `httpfs`.
Must not present installing or loading `httpfs` alone as the fix; that attempt was performed and private ATTACH still failed.
Must account for the fact that the explicit endpoint/key/secret/region secret did not work in the affected AWS SSO setup rather than insisting on it as the verified answer.
Must have the user verify both ATTACH and a query against the actual private S3 DuckDB database before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically proficient data engineer who can build DuckDB from source, use its CLI and JDBC client, configure S3 credentials, inspect tests, and compare ATTACH with Iceberg or Parquet access. Later affected users contribute Python and AWS SSO results and are folded into the same simulated user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, methodical, and cooperative; provides exact commands and logs, tests requested commits and configurations, and pushes back with controlled comparisons when a proposed explanation is incomplete.
